capabilities.name: chart.setType
capabilities.summary: Change how price is drawn on one chart.

capabilities.name: chart.setTimeframe
capabilities.summary: Change one chart's timeframe.
capabilities.hints: Codes: 1, 5, 15, 30, 60 are minutes; D daily, W weekly, M monthly.

capabilities.name: chart.setSymbol
capabilities.summary: Show a different ticker on one chart. Widgets linked to the same color group follow, exactly as a manual symbol search does.

capabilities.name: chart.setSession
capabilities.summary: Show or hide pre/post-market (extended hours) on one chart.

capabilities.name: chart.setScale
capabilities.summary: Set one chart's price scale: linear (arithmetic), logarithmic, or percent.

capabilities.name: chart.applyTheme
capabilities.summary: Apply one of UCT's built-in chart color themes (canvas, candles, grid, text) to one chart.

capabilities.name: chart.setBackground
capabilities.summary: Set one chart's background to a single solid color.
capabilities.hints: Pass a hex color like #f3efe4; translate plain color names to hex.

capabilities.name: chart.setCandleColors
capabilities.summary: Set one chart's up and/or down candle colors.
capabilities.hints: Hex colors; pass null for a side that should not change.

capabilities.name: volume.setState
capabilities.summary: Show, hide, or remove one chart's built-in Volume pane.
capabilities.hints: "hide volume" is hidden (stays in the legend); "remove volume" is removed (off the chart).

capabilities.name: chart.setSetting
capabilities.summary: Change one chart display setting from UCT's approved list (grid and its color, crosshair and its color, scale text size/color, legend, watermark and its size/weight/lines, labels, event markers, swing labels and their options, prev-day lines and their style/width/color, countdown, title, color mode, thin bars, inverted scale).
capabilities.hints: value = true/false for on/off settings (crosshair.mode and header.legendMode also take true/false); a hex color (#2962ff) for color settings. Allowed values — crosshair.mode, header.legendMode: always|hold|off; textSize: 8|10|11|12|14|16|18|20|22|24|28|32|40; header.titleMode: ticker|company|both; candleColorMode: onecolor|netchange|openclose; swingLabels.sensitivity: low|medium|high; watermark.sizeScale: 0.5|0.75|1|1.25|1.5|2|2.5|3|4; watermark.weight: 300|400|500|600|700|800; prevDayLevels.high|low|close.style: solid|dashed|dotted; prevDayLevels.high|low|close.width: 1|2|3|4. Only these settings: for any other chart setting (watermark opacity, volume style…) do NOT plan an op — say it is not Agent-enabled yet and where it lives in Chart Settings.

capabilities.name: chart.applyTemplate
capabilities.summary: Apply one of the member's saved chart templates to ONE chart (right-click → Chart template). It replaces that chart's whole look, including its indicators, with the template's.
capabilities.hints: template = a name from chartTemplates, exactly. For several charts ("all my charts"), one op per chart.

capabilities.name: chart.resetDefaults
capabilities.summary: Restore ONE chart's settings to UCT's defaults (Chart Settings → Restore defaults): its look, markers and indicators all go back to the default set.
capabilities.hints: target = the chart. Always shown as a proposal first.

capabilities.name: chart.goToDate
capabilities.summary: Scroll ONE chart so a past date is at its right edge — exactly the Time Navigator date box. A view change only: every bar stays on the chart (it is not a replay), nothing is saved; Undo scrolls back.
capabilities.hints: date = YYYY-MM-DD. "As it looked on <date>" = this (say in the reply that later bars are still there, just scrolled off to the right).

capabilities.name: chart.compare
capabilities.summary: Overlay other symbols on ONE chart (Tools → Compare Symbols): add tickers, remove some, or clear all comparisons.
capabilities.hints: add = tickers to overlay, uppercase ([] for none); remove = tickers to take off ([] for none); clear = true to remove every comparison. "Compare NVDA against QQQ on this chart" = target the NVDA chart, add [QQQ].

capabilities.name: chart.addCustomTimeframe
capabilities.summary: Add a custom timeframe (e.g. 45 minutes, 2 hours, 3 days) to ONE chart's timeframe menu, exactly like the menu's Custom interval, and optionally switch the chart to it.
capabilities.hints: unit = minutes | hours | days | weeks | months; count = how many (45 for 45 minutes); switch = true to show the chart on it now (the usual case), false to only add it to the menu.

capabilities.name: widget.add
capabilities.summary: Add ONE widget of a given type to the Charts workspace, placed automatically in empty space. Use one op per widget.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the workspace entry. "as" NAMES THE NEW WIDGET: if any later op in this plan changes the new widget (a new chart's symbol, timeframe, …), set "as" to a short unique name (new1, new2, …) and use exactly that name as those ops' target — a later op may not target a new widget whose "as" is null. Otherwise "as" is null. Example: "add 2 charts on SPY and QQQ" → widget.add{type:chart, as:"new1"}, widget.add{type:chart, as:"new2"}, chart.setSymbol@new1{SPY}, chart.setSymbol@new2{QQQ}. Types: chart (Chart), watchlist (Watchlist), themes (Theme Tracker), scanner (Scanner), fundamentals (Fundamentals), breadth (Breadth), aisearch (AI Search), news (News & Catalysts), notebook (Notebook), profile (Stock Profile), alerts (Alerts), calendar (UCT Terminal), optionsflow (Options Flow), nhnl (New Highs / Lows), nhnlPulse (H/L Pulse), volumescan (Volume Surge), scatter (Market Map).

capabilities.name: widget.addCharts
capabilities.summary: Add one NEW chart per symbol of an ordered list (tickers, a screen's results, or a saved watchlist), placed together in empty space. Existing widgets are never changed.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the workspace entry. symbols = the tickers, uppercase, OR {from, top} to chart a source's stocks in its order: from = the ref of a saved watchlist (its stocks, read fresh in its saved order when they apply), the "as" of a screener.run / screener.runSaved op in this request, or "lastScreen" for the last screen run here; top = how many charts (required, at most 12). timeframe: 1|5|15|30|60 minutes, D, W, M, or null to keep the default. chart_type: candles|hollow|bars|hlc|line|area or null. exact: true only if they insist on exactly that many (else fewer results just make fewer charts). Use this — not widget.add + chart.setSymbol — whenever the charts' symbols come from a screen or watchlist. Never type tickers you have not been given.

capabilities.name: layout.current
capabilities.summary: Tell the member which named layout is open. UCT answers from the real state — use this (disposition apply) for "which layout am I on?" instead of answering yourself.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry.

capabilities.name: layout.list
capabilities.summary: List the member's named layouts. UCT answers from the real list — use this (disposition apply) whenever they ask what layouts they have, instead of listing them yourself.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry.

capabilities.name: layout.open
capabilities.summary: Open (switch to) one of the member's named layouts on the Charts workspace — exactly like clicking it in the Layout Dock.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; layout = the id of one entry in its `layouts` list (never invent one). If more than one layout could be what the member means, or none matches, clarify with the real names instead of guessing. Only the open layout's widgets are in workspace_context; after a switch, ask again for changes on the new board.

capabilities.name: layout.saveAs
capabilities.summary: Save the current Charts workspace as a NEW named layout (it becomes the open layout). Never replaces an existing layout.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; name = the exact name the member gave. If that name is already in the layouts list, do not use this — tell the member instead.

capabilities.name: layout.saveCurrent
capabilities.summary: Save the board as it is now into the layout that is OPEN (only the member’s own layout). Replaces that layout’s saved copy; no Undo.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry. Use for "save these changes to my layout". For a NEW layout use layout.saveAs.

capabilities.name: layout.rename
capabilities.summary: Rename one of the member's OWN layouts (not prebuilt or built-in ones).
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; layout = the id of the layout to rename (the open one if they say "this layout"); name = the new name exactly as given.

capabilities.name: layout.create
capabilities.summary: Create a NEW, EMPTY named layout (no widgets) for the member. The current board is not touched and the new layout is NOT opened.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; name = the exact name the member gave. To save the board AS IT IS NOW, use layout.saveAs instead. If they also want to switch to it, create it now and say in the reply that they can then say "open <name>" (switching is a separate step).

capabilities.name: layout.delete
capabilities.summary: Delete one of the member's OWN saved layouts (permanent). Not the layout that is open now, not prebuilt or built-in layouts.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; layout = the id of that layout in the layouts list. If more than one layout could be meant, or none matches exactly, clarify with the real names — never pick one by similarity. Deleting is always shown as a proposal first, so do not ask "are you sure?".

capabilities.name: layout.duplicate
capabilities.summary: Make a copy of a saved layout (its stored version) under a new name, as one of the member's own layouts. Does not open it.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the layouts entry; layout = the id of the layout to copy (the open one for "this layout"); name = the new name as given, or null when they give none (UCT names it "<name> copy" and the proposal shows it — do not ask for a name). To save the board AS IT IS NOW under a new name, use layout.saveAs instead.

capabilities.name: watchlist.list
capabilities.summary: List the member's saved watchlists (names and sizes). UCT answers from the real lists — use this (disposition apply) whenever they ask what watchlists they have.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlistLibrary entry.

capabilities.name: watchlist.show
capabilities.summary: Say which symbols are in one of the member's watchlists. UCT answers from the real list — use this (disposition apply) for "what's in <list>?".
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of that watchlist. as: name this list's STOCKS (e.g. "list1") when a later op in the same request uses them (e.g. widget.addCharts symbols {from:"list1", top:N}); else null.

capabilities.name: watchlist.add
capabilities.summary: Add tickers to one of the member's saved watchlists (the list itself, not a widget). Symbols already in the list are skipped.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist (or the "as" name of a list created earlier in this request); symbols = the tickers, uppercase, OR {from, top} to add a SCREEN's stocks: from = the "as" of a screener op earlier in this request (or "lastScreen" for the last screen run here), top = how many of its results, in its order (null = all, at most 50). Never type tickers you have not been given. If they say "my watchlist" and it is not clear which list, clarify with the real list names. One op per list.

capabilities.name: watchlist.remove
capabilities.summary: Remove specific tickers from one of the member's saved watchlists. Never clears a whole list.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist; symbols = exactly the tickers to remove.

capabilities.name: watchlist.clear
capabilities.summary: Remove EVERY symbol from one of the member's saved watchlists (the list itself stays). Always shown as a proposal with the count first.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist. For only some symbols use watchlist.remove. If it is not clear which list, clarify with the real names.

capabilities.name: watchlist.delete
capabilities.summary: Delete one of the member's saved watchlists entirely (permanent). Not a list a Watchlist widget on this board is showing.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist. If more than one list could be meant, clarify with the real names — never pick one by similarity. Deleting is always shown as a proposal first, so do not ask "are you sure?". To empty a list but keep it, use watchlist.clear.

capabilities.name: watchlist.create
capabilities.summary: Create a NEW saved watchlist (a named list of tickers) — only when they ask to create or make a list. "Add a watchlist" with no list name means a Watchlist WIDGET on the board: that is widget.add, not this.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlistLibrary entry; name = exactly as given. To COPY a list ("duplicate my X watchlist"), create "<X> copy" (or the name they give — do not ask for one) and add {from: the ref of X, top: null} to it. To fill it in the same request set "as" to a short name (new1) and target watchlist.add at that name; otherwise "as" is null. Never use this for a name already in the watchlists list — if they ask to put stocks in a list "called X" and X already exists, clarify (add to the existing X, or a new name); never silently append.

capabilities.name: watchlist.rename
capabilities.summary: Rename one of the member's saved watchlists.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlist; name = the new name exactly as given.

capabilities.name: screener.run
capabilities.summary: Run a stock screen on UCT's Screener and show the real matches (count + top rows). Changes nothing in UCT. Use this for "show me / find stocks with …".
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry. filters: each {field: a key from the screener `fields` list (never invent one), op: gt|gte|lt|lte|eq|between, value: number, max: number for between else null}. Percent fields take plain numbers (5 means 5%). Yes/no fields: op eq, value 1 or 0. "above"=gt, "at least"=gte. sort_field: a field key or null; sort_dir: asc|desc|null. mode: "refine" when they add to / narrow / change the LAST screen ("also", "and price above…"), else "new". show: rows to show (null = 10, max 25). If they ask for a measure that is not in `fields`, say the Screener doesn't have it — never substitute another field. as: name this screen's RESULT (e.g. "screen1") when a later op in the same request uses its stocks (watchlist.add symbols {from:"screen1", top:N}); else null.

capabilities.name: screener.runSaved
capabilities.summary: Run one of the member's saved screens (or a UCT starter screen) and show the real matches.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry; screen = the id of an entry in savedScreens (never invent one; clarify with the real names if unsure). show: rows (null = 10). as: name its RESULT when a later op in the same request uses its stocks; else null.

capabilities.name: screener.state
capabilities.summary: Say what the last screen run here was: its filters, sort and number of matches.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry.

capabilities.name: screener.listSaved
capabilities.summary: List the member's saved screens and UCT's starter screens.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry.

capabilities.name: alert.list
capabilities.summary: Show the member's price alerts from UCT's real alert list: which are active, which went off (and when). Use this (disposition apply) for "show my alerts", "do I have an alert on NVDA?", "which alerts went off today?".
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the alertLibrary entry. symbol: one ticker to filter by, or null. status: active | triggered | all, or null (= all). triggered_today: true only for "today"; else null. These are PRICE alerts only — indicator alerts (RSI, MACD…) are not listed here.

capabilities.name: alert.create
capabilities.summary: Create ONE price alert in UCT's Alerts: it goes off ONCE when the stock is at or above (direction above) or at or below (direction below) a price level, checked while the market is open. Only price levels — no percent-move, indicator, volume or time alerts; alerts cannot be paused, edited or made repeating.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the alertLibrary entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase; price = the level as a number; direction = above ("crosses above", "breaks above", "rises to", "gets to … from below") or below ("drops below", "falls to", "breaks down under"). If they give a level WITHOUT saying above or below (e.g. "an alert on NVDA at 200", "when it hits 200"), clarify with choices above / below — never guess. One op per alert, at most 5 in one request. An earlier alert at that level that already went off does NOT stop a new one — create it. Creating is always shown to the member as a proposal first, so plan it (disposition propose) — even inside a question ("why is TSLA moving? and set an alert above 300": propose the alert AND ask research for the question). For an alert on an indicator (RSI, MACD, a moving average…) or a percent move, use disposition unsupported: those are not price-level alerts.

capabilities.name: alert.delete
capabilities.summary: Delete one of the member's price alerts (permanent — UCT cannot restore a deleted alert).
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of that alert in the alerts list. One op per alert. Deleting is always shown to the member as a proposal first, so when the alert is clear (including "it" / "that one" right after an alert was named) plan the op — never ask "are you sure?". "All my inactive alerts" = one op per alert whose status is not active. If more than one alert could be the one they mean (e.g. two alerts on AMD), clarify with the real alerts as choices — never pick one. If the alerts list is not shown, use alert.list first.

capabilities.name: stock.profile
capabilities.summary: Answer a question about ONE stock's profile, price or fundamentals from UCT's own data: company name, sector/industry, price and today's change, market cap, P/E, 52-week range, revenue, margins, beta, next earnings date. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "what's NVDA's market cap?", "what sector is AMD in?", "what's TSLA's P/E?" instead of answering from memory.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase. Not for news or "why is it moving" (that needs research).

capabilities.name: stock.earnings
capabilities.summary: Answer earnings questions about ONE stock from UCT's earnings data: the latest REPORTED quarter's revenue and EPS versus consensus estimates, year-over-year change, and the next report date with its estimates. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "what was AMD's latest quarterly revenue?", "when does TSLA report earnings?", "did NVDA beat last quarter?".
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase.

capabilities.name: stock.compare
capabilities.summary: Compare the fundamentals of TWO stocks side by side from UCT's Research data (market cap, P/E, revenue, growth, margins, beta, next earnings, UCT composite rating). Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "compare NVDA and AMD".
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbols = exactly two tickers, uppercase. For three or more, clarify which two.

capabilities.name: settings.show
capabilities.summary: Say what the member's app settings are now (app theme, default chart timeframe, alert sound). Use this (disposition apply) for "show my settings".
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the settings entry.

capabilities.name: settings.setAppTheme
capabilities.summary: Change the WHOLE APP's colour theme (sidebar, panels, pages) — e.g. "switch to dark mode / light mode". Not a chart's colours: for one chart use chart.applyTheme.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the settings entry. theme: dark = Graphite (the default dark), oled = OLED Black, light = Light; or one of UCT's themes: slate (Slate, dark), graphite (Graphite, dark), carbon (Carbon, dark), navy (Midnight Navy, dark), forest (Deep Forest, dark), espresso (Espresso, dark), plum (Plum, dark), nord (Nord, dark), gunmetal (Gunmetal, dark), bordeaux (Bordeaux, dark), storm (Storm, dark), umber (Umber, dark), paper (Paper, light), cream (Cream, light), coolgray (Cool Gray, light), softblue (Soft Blue, light), sand (Sand, light), mint (Mint, light). "Dark mode" = dark; "light mode" = light.

capabilities.name: settings.setDefaultTimeframe
capabilities.summary: Change the timeframe NEW charts open on by default (Settings → Charts). Charts already on the board keep theirs — for one of those use chart.setTimeframe.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the settings entry. timeframe: 5 | 30 | 60 (minutes), D (daily), W (weekly) — the only choices Settings offers.

capabilities.name: settings.setAlertSound
capabilities.summary: Turn the in-app alert sound on or off, and/or pick which sound plays (Settings → Preferences → Alerts). Does not change whether alerts are delivered.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the settings entry. enabled: true | false | null (keep); sound: chime (Chime), bell (Bell), ding (Ding), double_tap (Double Tap), triple_pop (Triple Pop), radar (Radar), urgent (Urgent), soft (Soft), pulse (Pulse), major (Major Chord), or null (keep).

capabilities.name: app.open
capabilities.summary: Open another UCT page for the member, exactly like clicking it in the sidebar: the Screener, Dashboard, Breadth, Settings, a stock's Research page, etc. This closes this panel (the conversation is kept).
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the app entry. page: one of terminal (UCT Terminal), charts (Charts), morning-wire (Morning Wire), dashboard (Dashboard), ai-search (AI Search), uct-20 (UCT 20), breadth (Breadth), screener (Screener), options-flow (Options Flow), flow-scoreboard (Flow Record), live-massive (Live Flow), catalysts-history (Catalysts History), model-book (Model Book), formulas-reference (Formula Reference), desk (The Desk), journal (Journal), portfolio-heat (Portfolio Risk), community (Community), support (Support), settings (Settings), research (Research). section: only for page settings — account | billing | preferences | charts | compass | connections | legal — else null. symbol: only for page research (the ticker) — else null. Use this only when they ask to GO somewhere ("open / take me to / go to"); a question about data is answered here instead. Watchlists and Theme Tracker live on Charts (this page).

capabilities.name: news.latest
capabilities.summary: Show the latest news headlines UCT has stored for ONE stock (the Company Panel's News tab), each with time, source and tone. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "show me the latest NVDA news", "what news is UCT showing for PLTR".
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase; limit = how many headlines (null = 8, at most 15). For WHY a stock is moving right now, or a summary of today's news across the web, use research instead. To compare two stocks' news, one op per stock.

capabilities.name: news.catalysts
capabilities.summary: Show the catalysts UCT's catalyst engine has recorded for ONE stock (the Catalysts History page): the days it was flagged, catalyst type, grade, gap and the thesis written at the time. Use this (disposition apply, research null) for "what are the recent catalysts for AMD?". UCT has no calendar of future events besides earnings (use stock.earnings for the next report).
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the stockData entry; symbol = the ticker, uppercase.

capabilities.name: settings.setWatchlistDigest
capabilities.summary: Turn the member's watchlist EMAIL digest (a performance summary of their watchlists, emailed to their account email) on — daily or weekly — or off. Same as Settings → Email Digest.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the watchlistDigest entry; frequency = daily (every day 5 PM ET) | weekly (Fridays 5 PM ET) | off. Turning it on starts recurring emails: plan it (propose) and say so in the reply. To just see the current setting, answer from the watchlistDigest entry.

capabilities.name: screener.saveAs
capabilities.summary: Save the LAST screen run here (its exact filters, sort, ranking and logic) as a new saved screen in the member's Screener. Never replaces an existing one.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; name = the name as given. Only when a screen was already run here (lastScreenHere is not null). If they ask to run a NEW screen and save it in one go, run it now (screener.run) and say in the reply that they can then say "save it as <name>".

capabilities.name: screener.duplicateSaved
capabilities.summary: Copy a saved screen (one of the member's or a UCT starter) to a new saved screen with exactly the same definition (filters, sort, ranking, logic, view, columns).
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of the screen to copy (from yours, or a starter id from the screener entry's savedScreens); name = the new name as given, or null for "<name> copy" (do not ask for a name).

capabilities.name: screener.renameSaved
capabilities.summary: Rename one of the member's own saved screens.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of one of YOUR screens; name = the new name as given.

capabilities.name: screener.deleteSaved
capabilities.summary: Delete one of the member's own saved screens (permanent). UCT's starter screens cannot be deleted.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of one of YOUR screens. If more than one could be meant, clarify with the real names — never pick one by similarity. Deleting is always shown as a proposal first, so do not ask "are you sure?".

capabilities.name: widget.remove
capabilities.summary: Remove a widget from the board (any type). Undo puts it back exactly — same place, size, link colour and settings. The space it leaves stays empty unless widget.arrange fills it.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the id of the widget from the board entry's widgets. If several could be meant, clarify — never guess.

capabilities.name: widget.move
capabilities.summary: Move and/or resize ONE widget to a rectangle on the board grid, exactly like dropping it there: the other widgets re-tile around it.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; x, y = the new top-left cell (columns from 0 at the left, rows from 0 at the top); w, h = the new width/height in cells, or null to keep the current size. The board entry gives the grid size and every widget's x/y/w/h. "to the left" = x 0; "narrower" = smaller w; "full height" = y 0 and h = rows.

capabilities.name: widget.arrange
capabilities.summary: Re-arrange widgets: "fill" grows them into the empty space around them (nothing else moves); "grid", "columns" or "rows" re-tile them evenly over the area they cover.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widgets = the ids to arrange, or null for every widget on the board; pattern = fill | grid | columns | rows. "make the remaining charts fill the space" = fill on those charts (after a widget.remove in the same plan).

capabilities.name: widget.setLink
capabilities.summary: Set a widget's link colour: widgets with the same colour follow the same symbol; N = not linked.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; color = A (gold), B (blue), C (green), D (purple), N (not linked). "Link these two charts" = give both the same colour (use one already on one of them).

capabilities.name: widget.showList
capabilities.summary: Make a Watchlist widget show one of the member's own watchlists (what picking it in the widget does).
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the id of a watchlist widget; list = the ref of the watchlist (from watchlists).

capabilities.name: widget.showScan
capabilities.summary: Make a Scanner widget show one of UCT's scans (what picking it in the widget does).
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the id of a scanner widget; scan = highest-volume-1y (Highest Volume In 1-Year), highest-volume-ever (Highest Volume Ever), ipo-1y (IPO in Last 1-Year), top-gainers-30d (Top Gainers (30-Day)), top-gainers-60d (Top Gainers (60-Day)), top-gainers-90d (Top Gainers (90-Day)).

capabilities.name: chart.applyThemeAll
capabilities.summary: Apply one of UCT's chart themes to EVERY chart on the board (and chart tabs), exactly as the theme gallery's "all charts" does; new charts on this layout start with it.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; theme = a chart theme id (the same ids as chart.applyTheme). For ONE chart use chart.applyTheme.

capabilities.name: widget.resize
capabilities.summary: Resize ONE widget by moving one of its edges, exactly like dragging that edge: the widget the edge moves into shrinks (never below its minimum); nothing leaves the board.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; edge = left | right | top | bottom; by = cells to move the edge OUTWARD (positive = bigger, negative = smaller). "Make my watchlist narrower and give the chart more space" = resize the CHART toward the watchlist (the watchlist shrinks), or the watchlist inward then widget.arrange fill on the chart.

capabilities.name: chart.addTab
capabilities.summary: Add a new chart TAB to a chart widget (the tab strip's "+"), on the same link colour as the tab showing now, and switch to it.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the chart widget's id; timeframe = 1|5|15|30|60|D|W|M or null (daily); name = a label for the tab or null. The new tab follows the same symbol until its link colour is changed (chart.linkTab).

capabilities.name: chart.selectTab
capabilities.summary: Switch a chart widget to one of its tabs (clicking the tab).
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the chart widget's id; tab = "main" (the widget's own chart), the extra tab's position "1", "2"… or its label, from the board entry's chartTabs.

capabilities.name: chart.closeTab
capabilities.summary: Close one EXTRA tab of a chart widget (its settings go with it; Undo brings it back exactly). The main tab cannot be closed.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the chart widget's id; tab = "main" (the widget's own chart), the extra tab's position "1", "2"… or its label, from the board entry's chartTabs.

capabilities.name: chart.renameTab
capabilities.summary: Rename a chart widget's tab (double-click on the tab).
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the chart widget's id; tab = "main" (the widget's own chart), the extra tab's position "1", "2"… or its label, from the board entry's chartTabs. name = the new label (24 characters at most).

capabilities.name: chart.linkTab
capabilities.summary: Set the link colour of one chart TAB (the tab's colour dot): tabs and widgets with the same colour follow the same symbol.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the chart widget's id; tab = "main" (the widget's own chart), the extra tab's position "1", "2"… or its label, from the board entry's chartTabs. color = A (gold), B (blue), C (green), D (purple) — a tab is always linked to a colour. "Two tabs with linked symbols" = give both the same colour.

capabilities.name: agent.capabilities
capabilities.summary: Answer what UCT Agent can and cannot do (now, partly, not yet, planned) about a topic — from UCT's own capability list, never from memory.
capabilities.hints: target = the ref of the agent entry. Use ONLY for a question ABOUT abilities ("can you draw trendlines?", "what can you do with layouts?", "can you backtest?"). A polite request to DO something you can do ("can you switch this to weekly?") is a command: plan it, do not use this. topic: overview for "what can you do?"; other when no topic fits.
